page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz under KVM hypervisor. It features 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 hyperthreads per core, alongside 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The CPU includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It supports key x86_64 cryptographic and bit manipulation extensions including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and standard AVX, though AVX-512 instruction sets are absent. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 7 Gbps, and the server relies on attached remote block storage as no local instance storage is included.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core CPU execution, supported by a stress-ng single-core score of 2677.3. Multi-core performance remains within average enterprise boundaries, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core result of 8861.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 21235.7. Memory testing highlights strong general performance with a PassMark memory score of 2753.61 and cached read bandwidth reaching 1033.55 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached memory write throughput drops to 18.82 GB/sec, placing write memory bandwidth in the bottom 25% of benchmarks. For lightweight AI workloads, text generation for small 135M language models executes at a strong 307.15 tokens per second.

The 1:4 memory allocation ratio offers solid resource density for general cloud workloads without requiring dedicated high-memory or GPU-accelerated hardware profiles. The key hardware tradeoff lies in the lower uncached memory write speed and reliance on external disk storage. Given its processing metrics and 7 Gbps network tier, the ecs.g7a.4xlarge instance provides efficient operation for microservices, web application hosting, relational database management, continuous integration pipelines, and light data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 vCPUs powered by an 8-core AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM and 7 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on KVM architecture, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core CPU performance and high small-model inference speeds, while multi-core workloads fall into average industry tiers. A primary hardware tradeoff is its relatively weak uncached memory write bandwidth. The instance delivers cost-effective execution for general enterprise tasks, microservices, web serving, software build pipelines, and general database hosting.
